summary: A non-magical Criamon ritual of walking a maze while contemplating a problem to improve concentration, granting a bonus to a single subsequent roll.

label: Labyrinth of Strife
summary: A tangled structure of tunnels at the Path of Strife's Initiation site that magi can only escape by performing feats violating Criamon tenets of apt action.

label: Lacerta
summary: A Clan Arelie magus of an Iberian sept, parens of Natrix.

label: Lacuna
summary: A 'hole' within an urban environment where the Dominion does not dominate, allowing magi to cast spells without realm interaction penalties; may carry other auras.

label: Ladislaus
summary: A trusted companion of Roznov covenant who haunts the Prague slave market using his Magic Sensitivity to identify and filter out Gifted children among the slaves for delivery to Coeris.

label: Lady Godgifu
summary: The legendary noblewoman of a story seed whose lord promised to reduce taxes if she rode naked through the marketplace.

label: Lair
summary: A Minor laboratory Supernatural Flaw: a creature hides or hibernates in the lab, known or unknown (-1 Safety, +1 Warping).

label: Lake District
summary: The region where the covenant Ungulus sits in a carved tower on a ridge, and where Aquila rides the thermals in eagle form.

label: Lake Nemi
summary: A sacred lake in the Roman Tribunal in whose waters Huntress initiates may bathe on the Ides of August during the Eumolpid initiation.

label: Lame
summary: A Minor General Flaw in which both of the character's legs are severely damaged, requiring crutches and heavily penalizing movement and combat.

label: Lammergeyer
summary: The bearded vulture deemed by House Jerbiton the correct falconry raptor for magi; its bones make particularly good magical flutes and it has deep orange iron-rubbed plumage.

label: Lamp without Flame
summary: A Creo Ignem spell that creates a steady daylight-bright light with no apparent source, illuminating about ten paces across a point that may be a mobile item.

label: (Land) Regio Network
summary: A Minor, Supernatural Virtue giving access to an extensive network of regiones (e.g. in lakes, sky, or caves) between which the character can travel quickly.

label: Landed Noble
summary: A Major Social Status Virtue granting a character an agency prior to play; listed with a Resistance of 3 on the Resistance of Agents Table.

label: Languedoc
summary: A region of central southern France where Brother Julian wanders and preaches against the spread of the Cathar heresy.

label: Lapis Maior
summary: The legendary Greater Stone long sought by alchemists, said to convert pure base metals into gold.

label: Lapis Minor
summary: A Level 20 Alteration Reagent creating a reddish waxy stone whose touch purifies a precious metal from its alloy; called the Lesser Stone, distinct from the sought-after Greater Stone.

label: Lares Lore
summary: An Ability used by Vestals to interact with lares (household spirits, also called penates), domestic faeries of the home and community.

label: Large
summary: A Minor, General Virtue setting Size to +1 so the character is six to seven feet tall, with wounds in six-point intervals.

label: Larinda
summary: A young Ex Miscellanea maga of Dankmar (age 20), daughter and filia of Jiphella, with a sunny disposition and affinities for Animal, Herbam, Aquam, and Auram.

label: Larta
summary: A category of unGifted person afforded protection and tutelage by a Hermetic House; Hildegard of Bingen is cited as a Larta maga of House Jerbiton.

label: Larus Egg-Thief
summary: Clan Chief of Clan Maruhs, a wandering magus with a skua (seabird) heartbeast who haunts the coasts of western Europe.

label: Lasiq
summary: A Major, Social Status Virtue for an experienced Nizari Isma'ili assassin who has completed seven murders and commands a small band of fida'is.

label: Last Flight of the Phoenix
summary: A CrIg 50 spell in which the caster immolates himself in a white-hot blast doing +45 damage; an early version was found in Flambeau's own lab notes, used by magi with Greater Immunity to fire.

label: Latent Magic Ability
summary: A Minor, General Virtue indicating an unmanifested magical quality, more limited than The Gift, that may appear spontaneously.

label: Latent Magical Ability
summary: A Virtue granting uncontrolled magical talent; Torven's Latent Magical Ability causes wolf packs to come to his aid in the forest.

label: Latin
summary: The scholarly language ability; a magus can rewrite up to Latin x 20 levels of Laboratory Texts per season to make them usable by others, and literacy in Latin is required to write or copy Lab Texts.

label: Latin Empire
summary: The crusader-created state ruling Constantinople after the 1204 sack, the weakest of four powers feuding over the Balkans, whose Latin Emperor cares more for his home Flanders than the City.

label: Latin Quarter
summary: The left-bank Paris district of jumbled houses where masters and students live, a lawless place of books, learning, drinking, and gambling.

label: Law of Names
summary: A magical principle by which knowing a ghost's full name allows it to be summoned, as used in the Incantation of Summoning the Dead.

label: Laws of Edward the Confessor
summary: 12th-century English laws under which the King owns all Jews and their property, relevant to a Minority Boon covenant in England.

label: Laws of Hospitality
summary: The Rhine Peripheral Code rules, derived from German guest-laws, governing the duties of guests and hosts and entitling a magus to request hospitality at any legal covenant for a vis fee.

label: Lay to Rest the Haunting Spirit
aliases: Lay to Rest the Haunting Spirit
summary: A Perdo Mentem (General) spell that reduces a ghost or spirit's Might by the spell's level if it penetrates, causing the spirit to vanish if its Might reaches zero.

label: Leadership
summary: An Ability for commanding others; women raised to manage holdings always have Leadership scores, and the angel Seferiel has Leadership 7 with a specialty in magi.

label: League of Iconophiles
summary: The most powerful of the eastern Empire's transient magical leagues, formed to oppose Emperor Leo III's destruction of religious icons; its members are the ancestors of House Jerbiton.

label: Leap of the Fire
summary: A Rego Ignem spell (Level 10) that causes a bonfire to leap up to 10 paces in any direction, catching if there is fuel; a Targeting roll lets it deal +10 damage to a target.

label: Learn (Ability) From Mistakes
summary: A Minor, General Virtue granting experience points in a chosen Ability the first time per session the character botches or narrowly fails a roll.

label: Learn Chirurgy from Mistakes
summary: A Virtue commonly taken by empirici allowing them to learn the Chirurgy Ability from their failures.

label: Leather Ripper
summary: A Minor, Supernatural Virtue granting the power to destroy a group of leather objects, as a PeAn(He) 30 effect.

label: Leccacorvo
summary: The Genoese bank cited as a legendary money/banking income example.

label: Lech
summary: One of the three legendary founding brothers of the Slavic peoples, who continued on to settle in Poland.

label: Lecherous
summary: A Major or Minor Personality Flaw in which the character seeks sexual contact with as many people as possible.

label: Leczyca
summary: A covenant established in Poland in 1052 by refugees from Grand Silesia to reinforce the New Slavonic Tribunal's authority over the Slavic lands.

label: Legatus a latere
summary: A cleric authorized to act on behalf of the Pope with his full power; granted Divine Magic Resistance of 20.

label: Legatus missus
summary: A cleric with papal authorization for a single purpose; granted Divine Magic Resistance of 15.

label: Legendary Artist
summary: An artist whose Reputation reaches 11 and is taken by his muse into a supernatural realm, becoming an immortal being with a Might score and supernatural powers based on his Craft or Profession.

label: Legerdemain
summary: An Ability used by a thieving performer to pick a victim's pocket via a Dexterity + Legerdemain roll while the crowd is captivated.

label: Legion of Mithras
summary: A 13th-century mystery cult reconstruction of the ancient Cult of Mithras that teaches additional powers via Initiation; Castra Solis's shield grogs may serve it as Auxiliaries.

label: Lemnos
summary: The island where Hephaestus settled and took twelve forge-companions; site of a Forge of Hephaestus, a Verditius covenant (Ingasia), and an all-Verditius community.

label: Leo III
summary: The Byzantine Emperor who in 729 ordered the destruction of images of Christ and the saints and forbade crosses in worship, prompting the formation of the League of Iconophiles.

label: Leonardo Fibonacci of Pisa
summary: A reclusive Pisan mathematical genius (Int +4, Com +5) who discovered the golden section / Fibonacci sequence and wrote the tractatus Liber abbaci; his work can aid Aristotelian Magic Theory and Herbam research.

label: Leper Magi
summary: A small lineage within House Tytalus descended from Hariste and Epimetheus who draw magical strength from leprosy; powerful healers and longevity experts who are inevitably specialized in Corpus magics.

label: Leper Magus
summary: A Major Hermetic Virtue exclusive to House Tytalus describing the mystic legacy of leprosy passed from Tytalus through Hariste's line; grants Life Boost and lets the magus mortify his flesh to produce vis.

label: Leprosy
summary: A Major General Flaw representing the divine disease; it gives a permanent -2 Living Condition modifier and an extra Heavy Wound during Aging Crises, and prevents gaining a positive reputation.

label: Leprosy (Flaw)
summary: A Major Flaw gained by the victim of the leprosy disease, imposing a Living Condition penalty and reputation effects.

label: Leprosy, Hermetic
summary: A Critical Melancholic Disease caused by Hermetic spells, a rapid hideous wasting disease with a pungent rotting smell.

label: Lesser Benediction
summary: A Minor, Supernatural Virtue granting a minor blessing from a supernatural power, with examples like Gift of the Gab, Green Fingers, and Pricking Thumbs.

label: Lesser Enchanted Item
summary: A category of enchanted device requiring the Lab Total to be at least double the effect's modified level and to which Effect Expiry cannot be applied.

label: Lesser Expansion
summary: A Minor laboratory Outfittings Virtue: the lab is enlarged with some specialized equipment (+1 General Quality, +2 Upkeep, 1 Specialization point).

label: Lesser Feature
summary: A Minor laboratory Structure Virtue: the lab features a unique structure aiding certain lab work, granting +1 Aesthetics and 1 Specialization point.

label: Lesser Focus
summary: A Minor laboratory Structure Flaw: an existing Lesser Feature is the central focus of the lab, enhancing it but hindering unrelated activities.

label: Lesser Guardian
summary: A Minor laboratory Supernatural Virtue: a supernatural creature (less than Might 20) not the owner's familiar resides in and protects the lab (+1 Safety).

label: Lesser Horde
summary: A Minor laboratory Supernatural Virtue: a small group of semi-intelligent creatures helps in the lab (+1 General Quality, +1 Upkeep, +1 Safety, +1 Aesthetics).

label: Lesser Illusion
summary: A Minor laboratory Supernatural Flaw: one apparent merit of the lab is merely an illusion; a balancing Minor Virtue is taken but its effects are negated.

label: Lesser Infernal Power
summary: A Minor Supernatural Virtue for corrupted beasts adding 2 to Infernal Might and granting an Infernal Power that cannot have a Penetration total.

label: Lesser Limits of Hermetic Magic
summary: The boundaries of what Hermetic magic can achieve, resulting from Bonisagus' unfinished theory; the forest paths each lead to overcoming one of these limits.

label: Lesser Malediction
summary: A Minor Supernatural Flaw in which the character has been cursed by a supernatural power, with effects about as bad as other Minor General Flaws.

label: Lesser Power
summary: A Minor, Supernatural Virtue granting one or more at-will supernatural powers equivalent to Formulaic Hermetic spells of total level 25 or lower.

label: Lesser Purifying Touch
summary: A Minor, Supernatural Virtue letting a character heal a specific minor or self-recovering illness with a touch and a Fatigue level.

label: Lessini Mountains
summary: The mountains where the Alps cross into Italy, site of Dietrich Von Bern's ornate tomb filled with dragon-blood-enchanted arms.

label: Leucrota
summary: A mythical beast whose tongue provides a Shape and Material bonus of +6 to mimicking human voices.

label: Levant Tribunal
summary: A Hermetic Tribunal in the Levant; off Ascalon within it, a Muslim fleet was defeated in 1123, leaving the cursed dead of Ascalon.

label: Libellus
summary: The newest and one of the largest covenants in the tribunal, founded and led by Stephen Eruditus of Jerbiton; an unknown quantity in tribunal politics.

label: Liber abbaci
summary: Leonardo of Pisa's book (1202), a Quality 14 tractatus on Artes Liberales (arithmetic) covering interest, square roots, alloy percentages, and the golden section; reading it aids Herbam research and Aristotelian Magic Theory.

label: Liber de Lumine
summary: A Tractatus on Ignem (Quality 11) by Elaine concentrating on light as an aspect of the Form of Ignem.

label: Libuse
summary: The Gifted granddaughter of Czech who had a great vision at Vysehrad Rock foretelling her husband Premysl, founder of Bohemia's ruling dynasty.

label: License of Absence
summary: A Major, General Virtue for a priest relieved of some duties, giving an extra free season each year; only available to Priest Social Status.

label: Liege
summary: A prince-bishopric and market city where the River Legia joins the Meuse, grown from the martyrdom site of St. Lambert; its most famous bishop was Notger.

label: Life Boost
summary: A Minor, Hermetic Virtue letting a magus boost Formulaic or Ritual spell casting totals by +5 per additional Fatigue level spent, risking damage.

label: Life-Linked Art
summary: A Major Supernatural Virtue letting an artist wound himself while working to increase artwork's Aesthetic Quality, making the piece a permanent Arcane Connection.

label: Life-Linked Spontaneous Magic
summary: A Major, Hermetic Virtue letting a magus produce stronger spontaneous magic at the cost of declaring an effect level and spending Fatigue or taking wounds.

label: Lifting the Dangling Puppet
summary: A Rego Corpus spell (Level 15) that lifts a person of Size +1 or less vertically into the air.

label: Ligature
summary: A small charm of parchment, stones, or herbs worn around the neck containing an Arcane or Sympathetic Connection, employing natural principles to grant a bonus to a single die roll.

label: Light Shaft of the Night
summary: A Rego Ignem spell (Level 20) that collects moonbeams and starlight into a controllable vertical shaft of soft silvery light, castable only under the night sky.

label: Light Touch
summary: A Virtue improving fine manual work; held by the Craftsman template and offered as an alternative for the Spying Maid.

label: Lightless
summary: A Minor laboratory Supernatural Flaw: the lab is totally dark and its contents cannot be seen, requiring other means of spatial perception (-1 Upkeep, +1 Warping).

label: Lightning Reflexes
summary: A Virtue granting superior reflexes, cited in connection with the adder's reflexive attacks and listed as suitable for beasts.

label: Limes
summary: A line of defensive forts reinforced by magic built by the Roman legions under Mercurian guidance, delineating the empire's northern extent and first fracturing the Hercynian Forest.

label: Limit of Arcane Connections
summary: A Hermetic limit concerning the use of Arcane Connections; a Touch-range spell on a room does not violate it even when affecting unseen people within.

label: Limit of the Divine
summary: One of the two fundamental limits of Hermetic magic: magic cannot affect the Divine, with most lesser limits believed to derive from it.

label: Limit of the Lunar Sphere
summary: A boundary of Hermetic magic at the orbit of the moon; magic cannot affect the moon or the ethereal region beyond it, and it stunts spells reaching toward the heavens.

label: Limits of Magic
summary: The fundamental boundaries constraining Hermetic magic; Major Breakthroughs push them, Hermetic Breakthroughs break Lesser Limits such as the Limit of Magic Resistance.

label: Lincoln
summary: An important town and seat of a powerful bishop, left in poor material state by the battle of Lincoln in 1217; its castle is held by Nicola de Hay.

label: Linden Gild
summary: A peace-striving go-between gild founded by former magi of Fengheld after the Schism War, seeking cooperation between magi and covenants; led by Occultes of Durenmar.

label: Line of Muj
summary: A mythic lineage from the Balkans whose ancestor made a pact with a magical guardian spirit, blessing his descendants with great strength and power over storms; surviving members live in the Transylvanian Tribunal and belong to House Tremere.

label: Lineage of Hercynius
summary: A Bonisagus lineage descended from Hercynius, the penultimate apprentice of Bonisagus, which founded Waldherz to pursue primal forest magic and was largely destroyed in the Schism War.

label: Lineage of Irmele
summary: A line of wandering, weather-working magi within House Bonisagus founded by Irmele filia Trianoma, prominent among the peregrinatores and the Linden Gild.

label: Lingering Injury
summary: A Minor General Flaw in which an old injury won't heal, penalizing physical rolls and worsening with age.

label: Linguist
summary: A Minor, General Virtue increasing all Language Advancement Totals and character-generation language experience by a quarter.

label: Lion of the North
summary: An Ars Magica sourcebook describing Pralix's war against Dav'nalleous, referenced in-text.

label: Little William
summary: A Redcap over six feet tall and heavily built who obtained a longevity potion; the only Redcap to wear armor (enchanted lighter chainmail) and a skilled fighter.

label: Living
summary: A Minor laboratory Supernatural Flaw: the lab's structure is alive, e.g. inside a faerie tree or the belly of a slumbering beast (-2 Safety, +2 Warping).

label: (Living Language)
summary: A General Ability representing fluency in a particular living language, measured on a fluency scale from point-and-grunt to elegant.

label: Living Quarters
summary: A Minor laboratory Outfittings Virtue: the lab contains furniture so the owner can live and sleep in it, a small benefit to lab work but bad for health.

label: Livonian Order of the Knights of the Sword
aliases: Livonian Order of the Knights of the Sword
summary: A crusading military order formed in 1202 in Pomerania and Livonia to fight Baltic pagans; reprimanded and subsumed into the Teutonic Order in 1237.

label: Llewellyn
summary: The last primus of House Diedne, last seen at Bryn-Celli-Ddu, whose parting words (Llewellyn's Curse) are carved into the passage wall there.

label: Llewellyn's Curse
summary: The carved parting words of Llewellyn, last primus of House Diedne, vowing that the House will last and return to haunt its enemies as long as nature endures.

label: Llewelyn
summary: The last primus of House Díedne, whose name fueled magi's belief that Gruffyd ap Llewelyn was a returned Díedne magus.

label: Llywelyn
summary: The prince of Wales who nominally acknowledges Henry as lord but controls south Wales and wages low-level war on the Anglo-Norman Marcher barons.

label: Llywelyn ab Iorwerth
summary: Prince of Gwynedd since 1194, a great warrior and politician who has come nearer than anyone since the Romans to unifying Wales.

label: Lochoch of Fox Lungs
summary: A Theriac of Level 20, Potency Strong, a syrupy medicine made from boiled honey that cures phthisis, a Major phlegmatic disease, over a month.

label: Locksmiths' Guild
summary: The guild of locksmiths, which historically did not develop until the late 14th and early 15th centuries; in the 13th century locks are made by specialist smiths.

label: Lohengrin
summary: The golden-haired knight drawn by a swan who defeated Telramund and wedded Elsa on condition she never ask his name; he departed when she finally did. His legend forms part of Wolfram von Eschenbach's Parzival.

label: Loire
summary: A river near whose mouth an island was a college for Druidic priestesses in the years before the formation of the Order.

label: Loki
summary: The multi-faceted and often malevolent Norse god from whom some Ex Miscellanea claim the Nemthengacha tradition descends.

label: London
summary: The principal English city whose ruling aldermen seek to increase the freedoms of the city; a center of specialized crafts and home to round churches and vagabond clerks.

label: Long Meg and Her Daughters
summary: A roughly hundred-meter stone circle in the Lake District whose stones cannot be reliably counted and are thought to be the petrified bodies of a witch and her daughters; Long Meg is a sandstone pillar that bleeds if chipped.

label: Long-Winded
summary: A Minor Virtue acquirable by a Bjornaer inner heartbeast and suitable for beasts such as the wild goat, horse, and wolf.

label: Long Winded
summary: A Virtue possessed by all Rottweiler grogs.

label: Longevity Ritual
summary: A ritual that slows a magus's aging, prolonging life across centuries at the cost of fertility and warping.

label: Look at Me
summary: A Creo Mentem spell that creates a thought in a target's imagination, causing him to look directly at the caster and make eye contact.

label: Loose Magic
summary: A Minor Hermetic Flaw that halves the magus's Advancement Total whenever he tries to Master spells.

label: Lord Guigues of Dauphiné
summary: A noble who commissioned Hephaestion to build a mechanized tin magpie automaton for his bedchamber.

label: Lord Marsyne
summary: A faerie lord (Might 50, Aquam) ruling an ice castle in the far north, who entombs people in ice, grants youth, and always takes a beautiful young human wife who must come of her own free will.

label: Lord of the Trees
summary: A Rego Herbam spell (Level 25) that causes a tree to move its branches and bend its trunk as mentally directed; a large tree gains Initiative, Attack, and Damage scores.

label: Lord Robert Schonburg
summary: Bastard son of Baron Schonburg and a diabolist who collects unjust tolls from Pfalz Island; an infernalist villain who casts ritual-like spells using Infernal Lore.

label: Lore-master
summary: A covenfolk template scholar versed in many Lore Abilities including Arcane Lores such as Dominion, Faerie, Infernal, Magic, and Order of Hermes Lore.

label: Lorelei
summary: A nymph that haunts the Rhine and sings men to their doom.

label: Loreley
summary: A beautiful, malevolent water faerie (Faerie Might 30, Aquam) who lures sailors to their deaths from the cliffs of the Rhine Gorge with her song; daughter of the Rhine Spirit.

label: Lorris
summary: A small town in France first granted customary rights by King Louis VI, later confirmed by Louis VII in 1155, whose generous customs included freeman status after a year and a day.

label: Loss of But a Moment's Memory
aliases: Loss of But a Moment's Memory
summary: A spell that removes up to five continuous minutes from a target's memory, leaving a blank focused on a specific event or time.

label: Lost in the Memory
summary: A Muto Mentem spell that fills the target's mind with memory, causing him to relive past scenes while neglecting all but basic urges.

label: Lost Love
summary: A Flaw often developed by Path of Strife magi who lose the spouses they married in the ritual at the Station That Repels and Attracts Elements.

label: Lotharingia
summary: The middle kingdom of the divided Carolingian empire that belonged to Lothar, later reabsorbed into Germany and divided into Upper and Lower Lorraine.

label: Lotharingian Tribunal
summary: A proposed separate Tribunal sought by members of the Apple Gild to cover the Low Countries in the north and west of the Rhine Tribunal, to be proposed at the Grand Tribunal of 1228.

label: Louis of France
summary: The French prince who invaded England with an army in the civil war and controlled much of southern England before being driven out by William Marshal as regent.

label: Lousy Ingredients
summary: A Free laboratory Outfittings Flaw: the lab is supplied with dirty, impure, or poor-quality ingredients (-1 General Quality, -1 Upkeep).

label: Low Ceiling
summary: A Free laboratory Structure Flaw: the ceiling is below the requisite ten feet, hampering some magical activities (-1 General Quality, -1 Safety, -1 Aesthetics).

label: Low Self-Esteem
summary: A Flaw common among Bjornaer magi who were catuli (apprentices ordered around) for most of their apprenticeships.

label: Low Tolerance
summary: A Minor General Flaw in which the character cannot easily withstand pain and fatigue, increasing related penalties.

label: Lower Lorraine
summary: The lower half of the ancient kingdom of Lotharingia, fractured into counties and duchies including the rival duchies of Brabant and Limburg, with forested uplands of the Ardennes and Eifel.

label: Lucas
summary: A magus of the Waddenzee covenant whom Imanitos got on well with during his stay there.

label: Lucas von Beck
summary: An aggressive Follower of Flambeau at Waddenzee (age 45), son of a German altgraf and expert in Perdo magics who has begun studying necromancy using bodies from his pirate raids.

label: Lucca
summary: A city in northern Italy granted a charter by Henry IV in 1081, overthrown in a commune revolt in 1115, which has since conquered neighboring lands and rivals Pisa.

label: Lucian
summary: An elder House Merinita magus of the covenant of Aegea in the Theban Tribunal, renowned for knowledge of Byzantine and ancient Greek literature and rumored initiated into story magic.

label: Lucidia of Flambeau
summary: A young Flambeau maga, one of the newly arrived members of Libellus.

label: Luck
summary: A Minor General Virtue granting +1 to +3 on rolls in situations governed by luck rather than skill, making the character do well at games of chance.

label: Luctatio
summary: A covenant in the Roman Tribunal between Milan and Verona, founded in 1172, heavily involved in Lombard politics; its Tytalus magi aided Milan against Barbarossa.

label: Lucy
summary: The wife of the Redcap Perceval, living at Mercer House with their children; she believes their daughter Maud has the Gift.

label: Ludold
summary: The white-haired elder of Waldheim, a lesser hedge wizard and cunning man who creates minor potions and charms; father of Torven.

label: Lug
summary: The Celtic and Gallic god of trade and commerce, also a sun deity associated with war, crafts, poetry, music, and magic, known as Lleu, Lugh, and Lugus.

label: Lumen of Jerbiton
summary: A young Jerbiton maga and obsessive bibliophile responsible for Schola Pythagoranis's library, who owns a ring that makes her appear as a man.

label: Lumen's ring
summary: A ring possessed by Lumen of Jerbiton that makes her appear as a man, allowing her to travel to monasteries in disguise.

label: Lunar Sphere
summary: The lowest of the celestial spheres carrying the heavenly bodies around the stationary Earth in Mythic Europe's medieval physics; it is also the limit of the power of Hermetic magic.

label: Luneburg
summary: A wealthy city built on extensive salt mines, where subsidence causes houses to tilt over rickety streets.

label: Lungs of the Fish
summary: A Muto Aquam spell (Level 20) with an Auram requisite that turns water into air as it enters the lungs, allowing the caster to breathe water.

label: Lupercus
summary: Ulf's ancestor who haunts the Bielowezca Forest as an immense wolf Great Beast and may impart the secret of the Inner Heartbeast.

label: Lupersus
summary: A Divine creature (Might 20, Animal) appearing as a noble silver-gray wolf sent by God to guard a holy hermit, provide food, and lead those in need to him; not an angel.

label: Lupus (the Wolf)
summary: A Minor Social Status Virtue for a character employed by a university to ensure students speak only Latin, holding keys to the students' housing.

label: Lust for Life
summary: A Major Curse (Creo Mentem effect) making the victim obsessed with sensual pleasure, requiring rolls to do anything besides follow compulsions.

label: Lutisse
summary: A very slight (Size -1) maga of House Ex Miscellanea who resides in a faerie-glamour-shrouded treehouse at the edge of a faerie forest.

label: Lux Draconis
summary: An undistinguished covenant founded in 915 in the Pennines; barely clinging to survival, it died out by 1100 and Blackthorn claimed its property.

label: Lycanthrope
summary: A Flaw causing loss of control over an inner heartbeast for a few nights each month; some Great Beasts inflict it on their Initiates, and it is a major hindrance within House Bjornaer.

label: Lymphae
summary: Water elementals (the 'pure waters') rarefied only from naturally occurring liquids; the best learners among elementals, they collect and mix substances and attack by pulling foes down to smother them.

label: Lyonesse
summary: A drowned land that once stretched from Cornwall to the Scilly Isles, Tristan's birthplace, sunk by the anger of the Fair Folk; its town was called Lyon and its remains can be seen at low tide.

label: Maddenhofen Woods
summary: A stretch of woods on the northwestern fringe of the Bohemian Forest protected by House Merinita; site of Tytalus's 807 AD disappearance and home of a powerful faerie who grants Heart's Desire at a price.

label: Madrasah
summary: An Islamic higher-education school attached to a mosque and run by religious leaders, privately endowed and supported by student tuition.

label: Maenads
summary: Women devoted to Dionysus who tore Orpheus limb from limb in a wild rampage.

label: Magdeburg
summary: A city on the Elbe favored by Otto the Great, seat of an archbishopric and center of missionary activity over the Eastern Marches; origin of the Magdeburg Law.

label: Magi of Hermes
summary: An Ars Magica supplement containing 15 fully statted magi at various ages, usable as NPCs or player characters.

label: Magi Orbi
summary: Magi who began in a different House but were exiled and found refuge in House Ex Miscellanea; they retain their former House's rules but lose its privileges and secrets.

label: Magian Lineage
summary: A Minor or Major General Virtue making the character a true blood descendant of the Median tribe of Magians, the original priestly caste of Persia, granting bonuses to aging and disease resistance.

label: Magians
summary: The original priestly caste of Persia, of which the Median tribe of Magians were the true blood ancestors granting the Magian Lineage Virtue.

label: Magic Addiction
summary: A Major Hermetic Flaw in which the magus craves casting magic and struggles to stop casting spells until he drops from exhaustion.

label: Magic Item (Virtue)
summary: A Free laboratory Supernatural Virtue: a magic item is installed in the lab, granting Virtues, Flaws, or Specialization changes; treated as Minor if very large.

label: Magic Items
summary: A Minor General Virtue granting a Redcap 25 extra starting levels of magic items plus accelerated improvement, reflecting devotion to the House.

label: Magic Lore
summary: An Ability concerning knowledge of magical creatures and phenomena; used to resist Vulnerable-to-Folk-Tradition magi and to attempt re-entry against Banishing.

label: Magic Resistance
summary: The capacity to ward off magical effects, granted to magi chiefly by the Parma Magica.

label: Magic Sensitivity
summary: A supernatural Virtue that lets a character sense magical auras and presences; held by the Scribe template and offered as an option for the Minstrel.

label: Magic Theory
summary: The Ability that governs understanding of Hermetic magic: inventing spells, enchanting items and studying from books.

label: Magic Theory roll
summary: Library trap mechanic: a magus following uncorrected deliberate-error lab notes who fails an Intelligence + Magic Theory roll against Ease Factor 12 rolls as if he botched an experiment.

label: Magical Animal Companion
summary: A useful minor Flaw giving a character a magical animal companion; listed as a resource increasing an agent's Resistance Strength.

label: Magical Beast
summary: A creature of magic with Magic Might that can be created at high levels of Creo Animal, requiring requisites for its powers and a Vim requisite for its magical nature.

label: Magical (Being) Companion
summary: A Minor Story Flaw in which the character is accompanied by an intelligent magical being he must regularly look after.

label: Magical constructs
summary: Non-human servants at Ungulus, including human-form constructs, self-working animated brooms, knives and pans, warning bells, and invisible bound spirits serving as guards and messengers.

label: Magical Fascination
summary: A Minor Personality Flaw in which the character is intensely interested in supernatural and magical phenomena to the exclusion of other motivations.

label: Magical Heating
summary: A Free laboratory Supernatural Virtue: heating is provided magically, functioning as Superior or Excessive Heating without space and Upkeep cost.

label: Magical Lighting
summary: A Free laboratory Supernatural Virtue: lighting is provided magically, functioning as Superior or Excessive Lighting without space and Upkeep cost.

label: Magical Memory
summary: A Minor Hermetic Virtue allowing a magus to reproduce magical creations without keeping laboratory texts, getting the benefit of a Lab Text from memory.

label: Magical Mount
summary: A Minor General Virtue granting a mount or beast-of-burden with Cunning and a Magic Might Score up to 25 that obeys simple verbal commands.

label: Magical Oven
summary: A Creo Ignem 20 enchanted device shaped as an iron box encased in fire-brick whose interior becomes red-hot on command to cook food.

label: magical raven cloak
summary: A magical cloak carried by the Skinchanger spouse covenfolk character, associated with her raven Skinchanger form.

label: Magical Warder
summary: A Major General Virtue giving the character a magical being, such as a ghost, that watches over him and comes to no harm; designed as a magic character.

label: Magical Wolf
summary: A magical creature (Magic Might 20, Animal) resembling a slightly large gray wolf that watches over all wolves in its range, can split into a pack of duplicates, and instantly slay any wolf it strikes.

label: Magister et Artibus
summary: A Major Social Virtue (university master of arts) listed as a high-Resistance social status on the Resistance of Agents Table.

label: Magister in Artibus
summary: A Major Social Status Virtue for one who has incepted Master of Arts at a European university and completed compulsory teaching, entitling them to teach anywhere in Europe.

label: Magister in Medicina
summary: A Major Social Status Virtue for a character who graduated from a higher university faculty; the highest educational license in Mythic Europe, granting 300 experience points and Academic Reputation 3.

label: Magna Carta
summary: The great written charter of English liberties, settled at Runnymede; its 1217 reissue is enforceable in court even against the king and constrains royal power.

label: Magnantrum
summary: Covenant founded around 1111 in a cave under Salisbury Plain; disintegrated in 1187 due to internal disputes.

label: Magus
summary: A fully trained Hermetic wizard and member of the Order of Hermes; the central player-character type of Ars Magica.

label: Magvillus
summary: The domus magna of House Guernicus, in the Roman Tribunal, where Prima Bilera resides.

label: Maiden Castle
summary: A large set of hilltop earthworks south of Dorchester in Dorset, seemingly deserted but said in local tales to be a faerie stronghold where the fay may be met on the correct night.

label: Maimonides
summary: A Jewish philosopher who wrote The Guide for the Perplexed in 1190, a great summa on Jewish philosophy infused with Aristotelian ideas, sparking the Maimonidean Controversy.

label: Maintain the Demanding Spell
summary: A Vim spell cited as not eligible for the Rebuttal Mastery special ability.

label: Maintaining the Demanding Spell
summary: A Rego Vim spell that automatically maintains a concentration-requiring spell already cast for the duration of this spell, without the caster needing to concentrate.

label: Mainz
summary: Formerly the Roman city Moguntiacum, raised to an archbishopric by St. Boniface; its archbishop is Archchancellor of the Empire and primas germaniae, and its see is a Holy See with a Divine aura of 7.

label: Major Breakthrough
summary: A significant advance in Hermetic theory; the Aegis of the Hearth was a Major Breakthrough, while inventing variant parameters of it would require at least a Minor Breakthrough.

label: Major Magical Focus in Spirits
summary: A Major Magical Focus developed by Titanoi magi during apprenticeship, applying to all supernatural entities with a naturally insubstantial form including ghosts.

label: Maker of Textured Vessels
summary: A Minor Supernatural Virtue allowing a character to craft vessels with impressed mystical patterns that grant a +3 bonus in a single Ability to their owner.

label: Maker of Water Vessels
summary: A Minor Supernatural Virtue allowing a character to make magical water vessels whose drinker may swap an Ability score for the crafter's Craft: Potter score.

label: Male Guild Sponsor
summary: A free General Virtue allowing a female character to participate in any guild by attaching to a male relative's name on the roster.

label: Malediction
summary: A Flaw a sahir might acquire from botched dealings with jinn during apprenticeship.

label: Malignant Magus
summary: A Minor Story Supernatural Flaw where a Twilight-loosed piece of the magus's psyche manifests as an adulteration that attacks his enemies without his consent.

label: Malocchi
summary: A tradition of Italian magi within House Ex Miscellanea who practice the magic of Entrancement and are believed to bring terrible luck with their gaze.

label: Mamluk
summary: A Minor Social Status Virtue for a former military slave bought as a child, trained at a military school and educated in Islam, then freed on adulthood.

label: Manifest Sin
summary: A Minor Supernatural Flaw in which a past sin stains the character's spirit and is manifest to those who can perceive hidden things, penalizing social interactions.

label: Mannus
summary: Son of the god Tuisto, from whom the word 'man' derives, who sired the fathers of the three German tribal groups.

label: Manufactured Ignorance
summary: A Minor Story Tainted Flaw in which a group of minor demons sustains the tainted character's delusion by arranging supporting fortunate occurrences.

label: Many Marriageable Daughters
summary: A Major Story Flaw in which the character has many daughters and must participate in stories to marry them off suitably.

label: Marbaid of Flambeau
summary: A magus of House Flambeau whose wizard's sigil is connected to an obsession with blood, turning his water spells into gushes of blood.

label: Marcher Lords
summary: Anglo-Norman lords holding land in or along the borders of Wales, including the Marshals, de Braoses, Mortimers, and Bohuns, whose lordships function much like palatinates.

label: Marco
summary: A disreputable Redcap, frequently described as a liar and charlatan, who reports many strange tales of covenants.

label: Marcus Navicularius
summary: A Follower of Verditius (age 58) and the foremost shipwright in Lübeck, a master of Terram who enchants extremely large items such as ships for sale to other covenants.

label: Marcus the Valiant
summary: The ghostly gladiator leader (Magic Might 20) who haunts the Trier amphitheater, equipped as a hoplomachus and challenging visitors to duels to the death.

label: Margaret of Beverley
summary: An English-born pilgrim who disguised herself as a man and helped defend the wall when Jerusalem fell to Saladin in 1187, later becoming a nun at Laon; an example of a woman warrior dressing as a man.

label: Marguerite of Flambeau
summary: A beautiful but rude maga of House Flambeau, sole inhabitant of Fengheld's Fengheld House chapter in Cherbourg, who considers mundanes beneath her.

label: Mari Amwithig
summary: An example Merinita maga used to illustrate Charm Magic, Story Magic, and Symbolic Magic, who modifies spells with charms and tricks faerie lords out of their treasures.

label: Maria
summary: A young woman near Mount Etna who has the Visions Flaw, feeling an empathy for fire and able to predict the volcano's eruptions through her dreams.

label: Marie de France
summary: A twelfth-century poet whose twelve lais are the best-known examples of that form of courtly-love poem.

label: Marius of Tremere
summary: A magus of House Tremere whose version of Ball of Abysmal Flame causes the ball to make a loud bang on impact; his magical sigil is a gaudiness in his spells.

label: Marking the Territory
summary: A ReCo 15 Scent-Target spell that bars Corpus-associated intruders from a warded area marked by the caster's scent.

label: Martial of Tytalus
summary: A magus of House Tytalus who collects turtle shells inscribed with bellicose Latin quotations.

label: Martin of Pattishall
summary: The senior professional justice at the court of the King's Bench.

label: Martin the Alchemist
summary: An example philosopher and alchemist with Philosophiae 5 who learns and concocts the Cement reagent and writes Laboratory Texts for fellow alchemists.

label: Maruhs
summary: One of Birna's six apprentices, told to 'Strive,' from her own tribe, whose name means 'stallion' in Old Gothic; founder of Clan Maruhs.

label: Marut
summary: One of two fallen angels who, per the Qur'an, taught sihr (magic) to mankind to tempt them from Islam.

label: Mask the Odor of Magic
summary: A spell used in conjunction with a magically maintained persona enchantment to hide magical traces.

label: Masking the Odor of Magic
summary: A spell of magical concealment that hides the traces of magic, which Tabanus's Reveal the Magical Deception is designed to overcome.

label: Masons' Guild
summary: The only craft guild that operates internationally, whose members travel across Mythic Europe in army-like groups to build cathedrals, churches, and castles.

label: Master Bard
summary: A Major Social Status Virtue for a character who has spent at least nine years at an Irish bardic school and is a master of the trade, called an Anruth.

label: Master of (Form) Creatures
summary: A Minor Supernatural Virtue letting a character tame animals and unintelligent beings whose Magic Might is aligned with a particular Form.

label: Master of Kennels
summary: A Minor Social Status Virtue for a character who manages the kennels of a noble patron, responsible for training, breeding, and health of the dogs.

label: Master of None
summary: A Minor General Flaw in which the character cannot stick at a task for longer than a season, preventing reapplication of experience points to the same Ability or Art in a year.

label: Master (Virtue)
summary: A free Social Status Virtue specific to the Rhine, granting the rank of magister, the right to train apprentices, and the use of a retired magus's voting sigil.

label: Mastering the Unruly Beast
summary: A Rego Animal spell (Level 25) allowing the caster to command an animal to perform any act it is capable of by touching it.

label: Masterpiece
summary: A Minor Hermetic Virtue allowing a Verditius magus to keep the lesser enchanted item he made to pass his Gauntlet, with vis costs ignored.

label: Mateos, the Faerie Butler
summary: A child-sized faerie (Might 10, Herbam) who lives for drunken parties, serving intoxicating drinks from an endless barrel and encouraging people to embarrass themselves.

label: Mathieus of Constantinople
summary: A contemporary House Jerbiton Archmagus trained in Constantinople but long resident in Paris, who gave up the study of magic but grew more active after Constantinople's fall.

label: Matilda
summary: A noblewoman trained in warfare who championed the Pope during the Investiture Controversy and led armies that all but destroyed Imperial authority in Northern Italy; an example of political-success-based female power.

label: Matthew II
summary: The duke who succeeds Dietrich III as duke of Upper Lorraine in 1220.

label: Mattieus of Cherson
summary: A historically important twelfth-century Primus of House Jerbiton who believed Jerbiton magi should serve as ambassadors to the mundanes.

label: Maud (daughter of Perceval)
summary: The two-year-old daughter of the Redcap Perceval and Lucy, suspected of having the Gift.

label: Mausoleum of Herlicarnasus
summary: An epic site chosen as the headquarters of the example league The Singers in Hollow Rooms.

label: Maximianus of Bonisagus
summary: An ancient, widely respected Bonisagus master of Corpus magic and prolific author who founded Nigrasaxa to break the cycle of invalid tribunals.

label: Mazdean Priest
summary: A Minor Social Status Virtue for an ordained Mazdean priest, initiated as a mobed, who performs Zoroastrian rituals and tends sacred fires.

label: Mecklenburg
summary: A region whose nobility still secretly come to Rethra to honor their god; its Slavic princes are drawn into the schemes of Radegast.

label: Meddler
summary: A Major or Minor Personality Flaw in which the character wastes time and energy trying to fix other people's lives, who usually resent it.

label: Medicine
summary: The academic Ability for establishing preventative health regimes and curing diseases, requiring knowledge of anatomy, physiology, and the non-naturals; used for diagnosis and prognosis.

label: Medicus
summary: A general term for a practitioner who may perform medicine or surgery but has no formal claim to the higher title of doctor; the majority of practicing physicians.

label: Medieval Universities
summary: Autonomous corporations of masters and scholars seeking independence from ecclesiastical and secular authority; in 1220 there are nine, organized into faculties, nations, and hospices.

label: Meles of Bjornaer
summary: A young Bjornaer magus, one of the newly arrived members of Libellus.

label: Melusine
summary: A water faerie whose blood is borne by the Breton Seirenes bards.

label: Memory of the Distant Dream
summary: A Creo Mentem spell (Level 20) that inserts a full false memory into a person's mind, revealed as false on a successful Intelligence roll; the memory vanishes when the duration expires.

label: Men-an-Tol
summary: A holed round stone with two pillars in a Cornish field, said to have healing powers (crawling through the hole) and divinatory powers (placing a gift and asking a question).

label: Menagerie
summary: A Minor laboratory Outfittings Virtue: the lab contains a collection of live animals (+1 Upkeep, -1 Safety, -1 Aesthetics, +2 Animal).

label: Mendalus
summary: A hierophant of the Huntress who in 1129 proclaimed at the Grand Tribunal that the Order should follow Merinita's true path; crazed by Twilight and believing himself the messiah, he was slain by fellow hierophants via Wizard's War.

label: Mendicant Friar
summary: A Minor Social Status Virtue for a follower of St. Francis or St. Dominic who wanders among rich and poor spreading the word of God.

label: Mental Construct
summary: A Major laboratory Supernatural Flaw: the lab exists entirely in the magus's mind via a powerful Creo Mentem ritual, limited by his Intelligence and unable to support familiar-bonding, item enchantment, or teaching.

label: Mentem
summary: Form governing minds, thoughts and emotions.

label: Mentor
summary: A useful minor Flaw representing a guiding patron; also noted as a relationship through which a character may be considered part of another's agency.

label: Mentored by Demons
summary: A Minor General Tainted Virtue letting a character learn Abilities faster than possible with human teachers, though demons only teach what suits their plans.

label: Mercenary Captain
summary: A Social Status Virtue that grants a character an agency prior to play and appears as a minor social status example on the Resistance of Agents Table.

label: Mercer House
summary: Powerful permanent magical gateways crafted by House Mercere, enchanted with the Hermes Portal effect; each connects to one matching pair, with hubs at Harco and Durenmar.

label: Merchant
summary: A Free Social Status Virtue for a character who lives by buying and selling goods, whether peddler, shopkeeper, or traveling merchant.

label: Merchant Adventurer
summary: A minor Social Status Virtue for a character in command of a ship and crew with sufficient capital for a cargo, though possibly with substantial debts.

label: Merchant Guild
summary: A guild of merchants granted by charter, holding monopolies (such as Ipswich's monopoly on milling) and operating a court for resolving disputes in towns like Freiburg.

label: Merchant Venturer
summary: A Social Status Virtue used to purchase the Typical merchant income band.

label: Mercurian cults
summary: Cults among the Hermetic magi whose members often succumb to the Vulnerable Casting Flaw.

label: Mercurian lineage
summary: A Hermetic magical lineage descended from the Roman priests of Mercury, granting Mercurian Magic and predating the Order of Hermes.

label: Mercurian Magic
summary: A Major Hermetic Virtue whose magical lineage descends from the Roman priests of Mercury, granting skill with Ritual Magic, free Wizard's Vigil, and halved vis requirements for Ritual spells.

label: Merinugalaudabila
summary: A Novgorod maga leading a nomadic family of faerie Merinitae who delights in certamen as a sport and has fostered interest in magical competition and dueling styles within the House.

label: Meririm the Meridian Devil
summary: A demon who commands the demons haunting the meridian region between the poles and rules an Order of Aerial Powers.

label: Merlin
summary: The greatest mage in the history of the tribunal, of mysterious birth and fate, connected with Arthur's rise; Hermetic opinion holds he was half fay, and he raised Stonehenge and enabled Arthur's conception.

label: Merlin's Well
summary: A spring on the escarpment of Alderley Edge in Cheshire, marked by an inscription and a carved face said to represent Merlin, where Arthur and his knights are said to sleep beneath the Edge.

label: Merovech
summary: A powerful 5th-century Frankish chieftain and wizard, namesake of the Merovingian dynasty, said to have two fathers and a magical bloodline; helped repel Attila at Chalons.

label: Merovingians
summary: A dynasty of Christian wizard-kings descended from the Holy-Grail-bearing Merovech and the Gifted Clovis; their corruption within seven decades is one proposed Divine cause of the Curse.

label: Merry Maidens
summary: A stone circle of nineteen granite boulders at Land's End, said to be girls turned to stone for dancing on Sunday to the music of the Pipers, who were demons.

label: Method Caster
summary: A Minor Hermetic Virtue granting a +3 bonus to the Casting Total of any Formulaic or Ritual spell, lost if the caster varies from his precise method.

label: Metz
summary: The largest and most important city of Upper Lorraine, originally Roman Divodurum, a wealthy Free Imperial City since 1143 and former capital of Austrasia and Lotharingia.

label: Michael
summary: A minor demon (Might 10, Corpus) who tempts people to wrath through elaborate, painful practical jokes disguised as the victim's friends, taking the name of the famous angel.

label: Michael Scot
summary: Named court wizard of Frederick II, the Holy Roman Emperor, cited as a Greater example of profiting from wizardry.

label: Microcosmic Station
summary: An advanced Station on the Criamon Path of the Body; Primi who achieve it are active administrators coordinating the House's ventures.

label: Midusulf
summary: One of Birna's six apprentices, told to 'Lead,' founder of Clan Midusulf, whose name means 'mead-wolf' (bear) in Old Gothic.

label: Midwife
summary: An almost exclusively female practitioner whose Chirurgy skills are employed throughout pregnancy and childbirth, sometimes having her thumbs surgically removed to assist births.

label: Mighty Torrent of Water
summary: A Creo Aquam spell (Level 20) that sprays a jet of water at a target, dealing damage and potentially sending them flying back.

label: Milan
summary: A north Italian city near the iron mines of the southern Alps, famous for armaments and its capacity to produce enormous numbers of weapons to order.

label: Mild Aging
summary: A Minor General Virtue granting a +1 bonus to the Living Conditions Modifier on aging rolls and a +3 bonus to survive an aging crisis.

label: Milo
summary: Second apprentice of Verditius who combined Boethius's philosophy with Germanic runes to invent Verditius Runes and discovered Hephaestus's torture chair at Ravenna.

label: Milo of Bonisagus
summary: An Archmage of House Bonisagus who prepared for his archmage contest while a member of Schola Pythagoranis, then joined Durenmar.

label: Mimer the Old
summary: A minor deity in the Scandinavian pantheon from whom Wayland learned smith-craft techniques.

label: Mimizan
summary: A covenant in the Provençal Tribunal with only two members, one of whom is the Praeco Dama.

label: Mind of the Beast
summary: A Muto Mentem spell (Level 30) with an Animal requisite that turns the target's mind into that of an animal of the caster's choice, with the victim acting like that animal.

label: Minerva
summary: A pagan goddess whose image in high relief is carved into rock just south of Chester and is said to continue to watch over the city.

label: Minnesingers
summary: A type of German minstrel copying the northern French style with emphasis on knightly combat and sensual love, exemplified by Walther and Wolfram.

label: Minor Enchantments
summary: A Minor Supernatural Virtue giving the character items with magical powers designed as Hermetic enchantments totaling 25 levels or less.

label: Minor Magical Focus
summary: A Hermetic Virtue narrowing and strengthening a magus's magic; the range of a Supernatural Ability is meant to approximate one, and it is required for the Beast Masters tradition.

label: Minor Potency
summary: A Virtue granted at the first Station of the Criamon Path of the Body, conferring potency in an aspect of the Art of Corpus.

label: Minor Supernatural Ability
summary: A Virtue granting a minor supernatural power, gained by long-lived Durenmar covenfolk in their seventh decade.

label: Miracles
summary: The direct intervention of God in the world, which can do anything, cannot fail, and cannot be resisted by any other power including creature Magic Resistance.

label: Miriam
summary: Flavius of Jerbiton's wife, of unclear cultural group and magical tradition; she attended the First Tribunal in an undescribed capacity and is buried beside Jerbiton.

label: Mirror of Opposition
summary: A Muto Vim spell cast on another spell being cast, causing it to have the exact opposite of its normal effects; ten Form-specific versions exist.

label: Missing Ear
summary: A Minor General Flaw in which the character cannot accurately locate the direction of sounds, suffering a penalty to hearing rolls.

label: Missing Equipment
summary: A Minor laboratory Outfittings Flaw: a lack of equipment makes one or two activity types totally impossible (-1 Upkeep).

label: Missing Eye
summary: A Minor General Flaw in which the character cannot judge close distances easily, penalizing missile, targeting, and melee attack rolls.

label: Missing Hand
summary: A Minor General Flaw in which the character has lost a hand, penalizing climbing, combat, and activities requiring both hands.

label: Missing Ingredients
summary: A Free laboratory Outfittings Flaw: a lack of certain ingredients severely hampers one Technique or two Forms, halving relevant Lab Totals (-1 Upkeep).

label: Missing Sanctum Marker
summary: A Free laboratory Outfittings Flaw: the sanctum marker is not prominently displayed or is missing, inviting Hermetic intrusion (-1 Aesthetics).

label: Mistaken Identity
summary: A Major Story Flaw in which someone who looks exactly like the character commits violent or embarrassing acts, forcing him to deal with the consequences.

label: Mists of Change
summary: A Muto Corpus ritual (Level 60) with an Animal requisite in which patches of mist transform anyone remaining in the target area into a random creature for a Year.

label: Mithras
summary: A luminous Persian-origin sun god worshiped by the Cult of Mithras as savior of Creation and divine Bull-Slayer; Castra Solis is named for his sun-god aspect.

label: Mithridates VI
summary: King of Pontus and enemy of Rome who employed Crateuas as court physician; his potions let him survive poison and torture.

label: Moat Monster
summary: A creature serving as a Local Ally for the Military Camp covenant situation, also referenced as a covenant Boon.

label: Mobile
summary: A Free laboratory Structure Virtue: the entire lab can be readily moved, e.g. on a ship or cart, usually taken with the Unstable Flaw (+1 Experimentation).

label: Monastic Vows
summary: A Major Story Flaw in which the character has taken vows of poverty, chastity, and obedience to a religious superior, as a friar, monk, or nun.

label: Monastic Vows (Hermetic)
summary: A Major Hermetic Flaw in which the magus has taken vows of poverty, chastity, and obedience, forbidding him from owning vis and limiting him to functional magic devices.

label: Monica Ierne
summary: The second-in-command of House Tremere, an Archmaga and master of combat magic originally from the Stonehenge Tribunal who serves as an excellent field commander.

label: Monstrous Blood
summary: A Minor Supernatural Flaw in which the character's essential nature has been changed through exposure to the Magic realm, giving her true form unfortunate supernatural properties and a visible deformity, while granting a -1 bonus to Aging rolls.

label: Montpellier
summary: A famed southern medical school where Gilles de Corbeil taught before leaving amid feuding with the faculty; one of the schools granting the Magister in Medicina.

label: Montverte
summary: A covenant in the Normandy Tribunal occupying a castle with curtain walls and mural towers, which it shares with its mundane lord and uses as a base for raiding permitted by that tribunal's Peripheral Code.

label: Moonbeam
summary: A Creo Ignem spell (Level 3) that causes a gentle reading-bright light to shine down and illuminate the area encircled by the caster's arms.

label: Morag
summary: A giant driven from his mountain home by diabolists who has taken to robbery near a covenant, holding a captured knight hostage in a cave; he craves revenge against the diabolists.

label: Moratamis of House Guernicus
summary: A maga of House Guernicus who, suspicious of Carolus of Tytalus, challenges him to certamen but ultimately concedes; an Intellego and Mentem specialist in the certamen example.

label: Moravia
summary: The eastern March of Bohemia bordered by the Carpathian Mountains and Hungary, through which flows the River Morava; home of the covenant of Roznov.

label: Morlen of Merinita
summary: A young Merinita magus among the members recruited to Nigrasaxa.

label: Mortuary Society of Kassala
summary: A society in Kassala, Alodia that makes Kassalan Dust and practices Kassalan Exorcism rites against ghosts and the physical dead.

label: Moses
summary: Biblical prophet referenced in the Divine setting material.

label: Motion Sickness
summary: A Minor General Flaw causing the character to become violently ill when riding a horse, in a cart, or sailing, doubling fatigue loss on long journeys.

label: Mount Blanik
summary: A mountain covered by a Divine regio, with an underground cavern holding the sleeping army of St. Wenceslaus, the Knights of Blanik, awaiting Bohemia's direst need.

label: Mount Etna
summary: A volcano on the island of Sicily beneath which the fire spirit Adranus slumbers; believed by the ancients to hold a gateway to the Underworld, it last erupted in 1194.

label: Mount Olympus
summary: The mountain home of the Greek gods from which Hephaestus was twice cast out; also the location of an all-Verditius covenant and a Forge of Hephaestus.

label: Mount Pilatus
summary: A mountain in the Alps where climbing can generate terrible storms, cited as an example of a Site of Weakness Hook.

label: Mount Purgatory
summary: A mountain commonly believed to sit at the center of the antipodal region directly opposite Jerusalem, atop Hell, a place of contrition and repentance.

label: Mount Radhost
summary: A 3700-foot summit in Moravia, site of a crude stone temple to Radegast with a Magic aura of 6 (secretly Infernal), where a great festival fuelled by human sacrifice yields vis for Roznov's magi.

label: Mount Saint Odile
summary: A mountain in the northern Vosges housing the convent of St. Odile and a holy spring with a Divine aura of 4, a place of pilgrimage especially for those with eye diseases.

label: Mountaintop
summary: A Free laboratory Structure Virtue: the lab sits at a mountain peak, a dramatic remote setting prone to winds and snows (-1 Safety, +1 Upkeep, +2 Aesthetics, +2 Auram).

label: Mournful Mound
summary: A hill containing the barrow of the Black Serpent, reached beyond the court of the sons of the King of Suffering, where Peredur slew the serpent.

label: Muirgheal
summary: A Quaesitor who led the Order's investigation into the Normandy restless-dead crisis and invited the Gifted Donatores to join the Order en masse.

label: Mummel Lake
summary: An enchanted isolated lake near Seebach in the Black Forest, home to a Nixe (water-nymph) whose jealous elemental spirits may slay the mortals she bewitches.

label: Munster
summary: A prosperous market and episcopal city on the Munsterland plain, founded as a monastery in 805 to convert the Saxons.

label: Muqta
summary: A Major Social Status Virtue for an important emir entrusted with an iqta', a feudal-like fief, following the Landed Noble rules.

label: Murion
summary: Prima of House Bonisagus and Praeco of the Rhine Tribunal, a powerful and overbearing archmagus who presents her plan to recolonize the Rhine Gorge to the new magi at the Forum of Durenmar.

label: Muse
summary: A title for any supernatural entity from the four realms that attaches itself to a prominent artist, granting Virtues, powers, and Warping in exchange for promoting its interests, eventually carrying the artist to its home realm.

label: Mustard Plaster
summary: A Theriac of Level 5, Potency Moderate, a linen cloth with ground mustard seeds that grants +3 to Wound Recovery rolls for Medium and Light Wounds by drawing out choler.

label: Mute
summary: A Major General Flaw in which the character cannot speak; magi with this Flaw take a -10 penalty to all spellcasting unless offset by the Quiet Magic Virtue.

label: Muto
summary: Technique meaning 'I transform'. Changes a target into something unnatural to itself.

label: My New Best Friend
summary: A Creo Mentem 25 spell of Henri de Tours that makes a target believe the caster is an old friend by substituting the caster for one of the target's real friends.

label: Myanar
summary: A figure who challenged Quendalon for leadership of the cult of Diana and was slain by him; his followers fled to House Bjornaer and founded the rival secret cult that became the Huntress.

label: Myrmecoleon
summary: A mythical creature whose exoskeleton provides a Shape and Material bonus of +6 to deprivation and starvation effects.

label: Mystagogue
summary: A charismatic Mystery Cult figure who commands a probationer and grants Initiation; Criamon usually use guides instead, though the Paths of Mirror and Strife use formal Mystagogues.

label: Mystery Cult
summary: Organizations that teach a mystery; four Houses of the Order of Hermes (Bjornaer, Criamon, Merinita, Verditius) are Mystery Cults whose members are Initiated into Outer and deeper Inner Mysteries.

label: (Mystery Cult) Lore
summary: An (Organization) Lore Ability for a particular Mystery Cult, covering its legends, history, structure, rites, secret passwords, and Initiation ceremonies.

label: Mystery of Ascendancy to the Hall of Heroes
aliases: Ascendancy to the Hall of Heroes
Mystery of Ascendancy to the Hall of Heroes
summary: The innermost Mystery of the Huntress, Initiated as the Chosen of Diana via a Quest to find and slay Quendalon in Arcadia, a great Sacrifice, and ritual blinding.

label: Mystery of Divination
summary: A Major Virtue acquired through Clan Ilfetu's Trial and Oath of the Prophet, alongside the Visions Flaw.

label: Mystery of Divination and Augury
aliases: Esoteric Mystery of Divination and Augury
summary: An Esoteric Mystery into which Clan Ilfetu members may be Initiated, teaching the haemagmomancy divination method.

label: Mystery of Hermetic Synthemata
summary: The Mystery into which a new hierophant of the Huntress is Initiated, vital to controlling the pagan messiah they hope to create.

label: Mystery of the Anima
summary: A Major House Mystery of House Bjornaer that transforms the heartbeast into a spiritual or elemental form composed of an element such as earth, fire, air, water, smoke, or shadow.

label: Mystery of the Epitome
summary: A Major House Mystery of House Bjornaer that perfects the heartbeast into a Beast of Virtue, granting Characteristic bonuses, Mythic Feats, and immunity to physical Flaws in inner form.

label: Mystical Choreography
summary: A Minor Hermetic Virtue letting a magus perform Ceremonial Magic faster (five minutes per magnitude, or one minute in a prepared space) through skilled body movement.

label: Mythic Blood
summary: A Virtue marking descent from a supernatural ancestor such as Birna or a Great Beast, granting a magical feat spell, a Minor Magical Focus, and a hereditary Personality Flaw.

label: Mythic Companion
summary: A powerful tier of player character that may take up to 10 points of Flaws and twice the normal Virtues, defined by a Free Virtue specifying which type of Mythic Companion they are.

label: Mythic Europe
summary: The setting of Ars Magica: an early-13th-century Europe in which the myths and superstitions of the age are literally true. Magi of the Order of Hermes wield potent magic from covenants hidden across the continent, while faeries, demons, angels and magical beasts inhabit the wider world.

label: Mythic Feat
summary: An automatically successful incredible action a Beast of Virtue may perform at the cost of a confidence Point, covering feats of Perception, Presence, Strength, and other Characteristics.

label: Mythic Germany
summary: The magic-soaked lands of medieval Germany within the Holy Roman Empire, birthplace of the Order of Hermes and setting of the Rhine Tribunal.

label: Mythic Herbalism
summary: A Major Supernatural Virtue and Ability that lets a character create healing unguents, poultices, virulent poisons, and physical-bonus potions.

label: Mythic Pound
summary: The standardized currency unit used for prices in Ars Magica, equivalent to a pound of silver, a typical peasant's annual income, or a year's upkeep of an average Hermetic laboratory.

label: Nameless Covenant
summary: A Díedne covenant established on an ancient druidic shrine on Anglesey in 817, destroyed in 1011 and stricken from the records by the quaesitores after the Schism War.

label: Names of Power
summary: A Mystery Virtue the Titanoi cult can Initiate.

label: Naples
summary: A city whose catacombs harbored the necromancer Guorna the Fetid and her tradition, which Tytalus and Tremere destroyed.

label: Narrowly Cognizant
summary: A Free Virtue indicating a faerie is aware of its faerie nature in a limited way; it tries to play its role accurately and cannot break role even unto death.

label: Nasir
summary: A minor angel of the Divine realm (Divine Might 25, Corpus) charged with the safety of pious travellers, who aids those in need before vanishing. He has powers such as Calming Touch, Spirit Form, Steadying Hand, and Subtle Form.

label: Natrix
summary: The filius of Lacerta in a Clan Arelie sept in Iberia.

label: Natura Antiqua
summary: A covenant of nature magi founded in the East Anglian fens in 1133, destroyed by Geoffrey de Mandeville during the Civil War in 1143.

label: Natural Environment
summary: A Major laboratory Structure Virtue: natural scenery such as forest, desert, or river is in or around the lab, granting Aesthetics and terrain-appropriate Specializations.

label: Natural Leader
summary: A Minor General Virtue giving a +3 bonus to social situations where the dominant character takes the lead, partly overcoming the social penalty of The Gift.

label: Natural Magician
summary: A practitioner of non-Hermetic natural magic; Amabel the Learned is one, as powerful as many Hermetic magi, and some churchmen have begun employing such magicians.

label: Nature Lore
summary: A Mystery (Virtue) Initiated by the Vestals with the unique focus of lares (household spirits), letting them interact with the faeries of a settlement as nature magi do with the wilderness.

label: Naumburg
summary: A well-fortified town high above the River Saale with its own bishop, beginning construction of a cathedral dedicated to St. Peter and St. Paul.

label: Nebelkönigin
summary: A magically enhanced ship, pride of Waddenzee's pirate fleet, stolen from Oculus Septentrionalis (built by the Verditius shipwright Marcus) while it carried vis and magical books.

label: Necessary Condition
summary: A Flaw imposed as a Great Beast's Ordeal requiring a condition for magic (e.g., a bull chimera touching the ground); also a common Bjornaer flaw when in human or heartbeast form.

label: Necessary (Realm) Aura for (Ability)
summary: A Minor Supernatural Flaw giving a -3 penalty to a particular Ability when the character is not in the appropriate supernatural aura.

label: Necessity
summary: The underlying laws of the universe in Criamon cosmology that forced the immortals into the cycle of time for three eternities.

label: Nef
summary: The main carvel-built trade ship of the Mediterranean, following a Roman design with lateen rigging borrowed from the Arabs and up to three masts.

label: Neo-Mercurians
summary: A Hermetic Mystery Cult interested in Roman ceremonies and culture, said to be related to the Cult of Mercury.

label: Nephilim
summary: A Mythic Companion type: divine giants and heroes of ancient myth, descended from angels, who age very slowly and dwell mostly in divine regiones. They require the Blood of the Nephilim and related Divine-aligned Virtues.

label: Nephilim (Virtue)
summary: The Free Mythic Companion Virtue defining a character as a Nephilim.

label: Neptune's Brooch
summary: A wondrous carved precious stone made by a jeweler that prevents the wearer from drowning by letting him float on water (Craft Level 14).

label: Neptune's Imprisoning Arms
summary: A Muto Aquam spell (MuAq 25) created by Falke that forms semi-solid 'vines' of water that can hold a small boat or up to six people, operating like Trap of the Entwining Vines.

label: Neptune's Wrath
summary: A Rego Aquam Ritual spell (Level 40) that creates a gigantic wave up to a mile wide capable of capsizing ships and devastating coastlines.

label: Nestor
summary: Iacob's faerie caricature, a white (albino) crow that accompanies him on his travels and identifies him as the Prophet of the God of Truth.

label: Nestor of Tremere
summary: The current curator (head) of the oppidum of Tablinum, who holds a collection of Arcane Connections used to enter its regiones.

label: New Aristotle
summary: The body of newly translated works of Aristotle dubbed by scholastic leaders, central to the twelfth-century recovery of philosophical knowledge.

label: New Forest
summary: A royal forest in England cited as a legendary forestry income example.

label: Niall
summary: The example player who creates the magus Darius of Flambeau throughout the Detailed Character Creation worked example.

label: Nibelungenlied
summary: The great epic poem of the tragic fate of the Burgundian people, immortalizing Siegfried, Kriemhild, Gunther, and Hagen, treated as true history in Mythic Germany.

label: Nibelungs
summary: A legendary race of men from the Lower Rhine who collaborated with dwarves and giants to conquer the wild river; their lost treasure is the Rhinegold.

label: Nicola de Hay
summary: The elderly hereditary constable of Lincoln castle and sheriff of the shire who held the castle through a siege and is locked in a conflict with the earl of Salisbury over her position.

label: Night Terrors
summary: A Minor General Flaw in which the character is plagued by horrible nightmares, requiring a Stress Roll against Ease Factor 9 to avoid terrors and Long Term Fatigue loss.

label: Nigrasaxa
summary: A relatively new, large covenant of two shining black towers, founded by Maximianus of Bonisagus to break the cycle of invalid tribunals.

label: Nike
summary: The Daimon of victory in both battle and peaceful competition, daughter of Styx and Pallas, invoked in an Orphic Hymn used in eristic moots.

label: Niobe
summary: A Criamon maga who longed to be Prima but was never selected; her perfect transmission created a study pond as she faded into Twilight.

label: Nixe
summary: A water-nymph faerie dwelling in the enchanted Mummel Lake who bewitches young men with her beauty, drawing the jealousy of the lake's elemental spirits.

label: Nizari Isma'ilis
summary: An order of assassins, far from whose home fida'is and lasiqs are sent on missions; fida'i and lasiq Social Statuses are drawn from this sect.

label: No Hands
summary: A Major General Flaw in which the character has no hands; magi take a -5 penalty to all Casting Scores, offset by the Subtle Magic Virtue or Still Casting.

label: No Sense of Direction
summary: A Minor General Flaw in which the character is completely unable to follow directions and frequently gets lost; incompatible with the Well Traveled Virtue.

label: No Stores
summary: A Minor laboratory Structure Flaw: the lab has nowhere to store supplies and cannot withstand shortages (-2 Safety).

label: Nocturnal
summary: A Minor General Flaw in which the character's body rhythms keep him sleeping until noon, giving -1 on all rolls between dawn and midday but ease at night.

label: Nomos
summary: In Tytalan philosophy, the abstract force of law, convention, or custom—a human invention that glues society together but is changeable and thus open to challenge.

label: Noncombatant
summary: A Flaw making a creature unwilling or unable to fight; possessed by the courser horse and the caladrius and listed among Flaws suitable for beasts.

label: Nortorf
summary: A small town in Holstein at the meeting of roads to Schleswig, Lübeck, and Hamburg, site of the prophesied infernal ash seedling cut down each New Year's Night by a white horseman.

label: Notary
summary: A Minor Social Status Virtue for a legal official employed by lords or towns who draws up contracts, witnesses charters, and affixes a seal.

label: Notatus
summary: The first Hermetic apprentice of Bonisagus, chosen as Primus of House Bonisagus and thereby the first Praeco of the Rhine after Bonisagus; his sigil is held by Murion.

label: Notes of a Delightful Sound
summary: A Muto Imaginem spell (Level 10) that causes all sounds in a room, particularly music, to be especially clear and sonorous.

label: Notger
summary: Liege's most famous bishop, granted the diocese as a fiefdom by Otto II, responsible for many of Liege's grandest buildings, after whom it became a prince-bishopric.

label: Notre Dame de Paris
summary: The Paris cathedral whose recently completed nave is 112 feet tall, with its chancellor wielding power over the university.

label: Nottingwood
summary: A town in a story seed that entered a charter agreement with a faerie king, electing a council of seven aldermen and hosting faerie merchants and knights.

label: Novgorod Tribunal
summary: A Tribunal bordering Pomerania to which Livonia and (officially) Denmark/Scandinavia belong; a region of contention with the Rhine over Pomerania and Baltic vis sites.

label: Nuntius
summary: A Free Social Status Virtue for a messenger charged with delivering messages, mail, and donations between students and families, employed by a university nation.

label: Nuremberg
summary: An important Franconian trading city at a crossroads of trade routes, home to the Kaiserburg imperial castle and an unofficial capital of the empire.

label: Oak Gild
summary: A political gild of the Rhine Tribunal that, in the Crintera Schism, aligns with the Harmonist Bjornaer to start a territorial dispute with Novgorod; Roznov's other magi belong to the Ash or Oak Gilds.

label: Oakdell
summary: A former covenant founded 934 AD by magi of House Diedne in the Westerwald; razed to the ground with all its Diedne magi slain during the Schism War in 1016 AD.

label: Oath of Fealty
summary: A Major Story Flaw in which the character has sworn loyalty and support to someone outside the covenant; magi are forbidden from such oaths by the Hermetic Code.

label: Obano
summary: A 25-year-old journeyman swordsmith originally from Aragon, strong and scarred, who holds evidence of his former master's illegal dealings.

label: Obese
summary: A Minor General Flaw in which the character is large due to fat, giving -1 to rolls involving quick or graceful movement and -3 to Fatigue rolls.

label: Object of Increased Size
summary: An enchanted item whose effect makes an object larger; a faculty's possession of one sparks a violent university debate over whether size is substance or quantity.

label: Obliteration of the Metallic Barrier
summary: A Perdo Terram spell (with Rego requisite) that shatters a metal or stone barrier up to one foot thick, harming those on the far side.

label: Obsessed
summary: A Major or Minor Personality Flaw in which the character is fixated on a prized object, action, or ideal that interferes with more immediate tasks.

label: Obsession
summary: A demonic power tied to a particular sin which the demon may impose upon a mortal indulging in a venial sin, granting the victim a sinful Personality Trait.

label: Occulta
summary: A covenant founded in the East Anglian fens in 893 by newly gauntleted magi; it failed to establish resources and collapsed in 897.

label: Occultes
summary: A Follower of Bonisagus and figurehead of the outward-looking faction favoring hedge wizardry; former librarian and now leader of the Linden Gild who secretly hoards restricted texts.

label: Oculus Septentrionalis
summary: A Rhine Tribunal covenant based in Lubeck, dominated by Jerbiton magi and merchants and lacking a Magic aura at its city site; deeply involved in commerce and the genesis of the Hanseatic League.

label: Odofredus
summary: A great debater at Bologna and frontrunner for rector of the Faculty of Law, rival of Accursius in completing a legal digest.

label: Odorpes
summary: A maga of House Bjornaer and filia of Urgen, sole inhabitant of Fengheld's Lusatia chapter, who spends most of her time as a bear and hibernates all winter.

label: Odysseus
summary: The legendary hero whose famous tale of resisting the sirens illustrates how the Seirenes' magic could be defeated.

label: Offa's Dyke
